title: Stigmatization campaign since the Robertson Panel

tellings.quote: Well, remember this this whole stigmatization has been an 80-year campaign and it's been very effective and wellunded. It started after the Robertson panel

The "debunking" aim would result in reduction in public interest in "flying saucers" which today evokes a strong psychological reaction. This education could be accomplished by mass media such as television, motion pictures, and popular articles.

a. That the national security agencies take immediate steps to strip the Unidentified Flying Objects of the special status they have been given and the aura of mystery they have unfortunately acquired;

plain: For eighty years, a well-funded campaign has made it shameful to take UFOs seriously, and it began in 1953 with the Robertson Panel, a group of scientists the CIA brought together that year to review UFO reports. That is the view of Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy rear admiral, who tells Michels the campaign "has been very effective." If true, it would mean the ridicule around the subject was planned rather than natural. The panel's report, dated 16 February 1953 and filed by the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence, does call for a "debunking" aim that "would result in reduction in public interest in 'flying saucers'," to be carried out through "television, motion pictures, and popular articles." It also recommends that "the national security agencies take immediate steps to strip the Unidentified Flying Objects of the special status they have been given and the aura of mystery they have unfortunately acquired." So the report plainly urges a public effort to deflate interest; whether that effort was carried out, funded, and kept going for decades, as Gallaudet says, is a step beyond what a 1953 recommendation can show.
